entries.title: ## 2026-10-02 (1 GPU hold + host build): T-GPLR-76 answers "which nodes" — the ONLY host-side op in the attention graph is VIEW, and VIEW executes no kernel. The 75% "mixed" was a telemetry artifact, not CPU inference. CORRECTS the T-GPLR-75 reading

## 2026-10-02 (3 GPU holds, 10 arms, bisect): the ~58 GiB commit hold is NOT ours and NOT context-driven — ctx is eliminated, the stock llama.cpp path holds MORE (70.6 GiB) than the streaming K=2 path (59.4 GiB) on the identical workload

## 2026-10-02 (1 GPU hold + host build): T-GPLR-75 answers the owner's CPU-inference question BY MEASUREMENT — the K cache is GPU-side, handoff-partial is CPU-side; and the RAM commit spike is localised in TIME (a flat 58 GiB step held for the whole run)

## 2026-10-02 (4 GPU holds, owner-directed TG focus): the K cache is MEASURED at last — TG 13.3-16.2 tok/s, peak VRAM 9,607.9 MiB so it does NOT fit 8 GiB; TG is 97.1% host-bound; `--kv-graph-pad 256` breaks TG on the row-set path; and a ~71 GB transient COMMIT spike whose first explanation was falsified

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, code inspection, no GPU hold): the K-cache was NEVER tested at our shape and is not wired into the layer-major PP executor — and the act slab is architecturally minimal, so "size it per chunk" is not available. The real 8 GB lever is q4 KV

## 2026-10-02 (ONE GPU hold, 4 arms, owner-authorised): the CPU thread lever is REFUTED on hardware — 1/4/12/16 threads give 30.116/29.577/29.979/29.990 tok/s, a 1.8% spread, where the microbenchmark predicts 66%. Host layer cost is thread-invariant at ~682 us

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): NUMA is ELIMINATED (1 socket, 0 NUMA nodes) and first-touch is RULED OUT BY MAGNITUDE (13x penalty vs the observed 1.68x) — what is left is thread UNDER-UTILISATION: 16 threads are configured, ~4 logical cores are busy

## 2026-10-02 (host-only analysis + one host build, NO GPU): the overlap question is ANSWERED from existing traces — ZERO host/device overlap in 4,992 layer transitions — and per-span `cpu_us`/`dev` telemetry is built to confirm it per layer (compiled, 77/77, not yet run on hardware)

## 2026-10-02 (HOST-ONLY microbenchmark, NO GPU, NO mutex): the 36.5us/expert figure REPRODUCES at 35.07 (12 threads) — and the in-situ 58.0us/expert is the 1-THREAD cell almost exactly, so the host is running expert FFN single-threaded on a machine that saturates at 12

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): the 42.6%-vs-4.0% blocker is CLOSED and the policy question it gated is answered — experts already run on the CPU, it is VRAM-forced, and the host is running at 30.5 of a possible 48.5 GB/s, so the gap is parallelisation, not bandwidth

## 2026-10-02 (host-only + one host build, NO GPU): pool hit-rate observability FIXED — the published rate's denominator excluded every capacity failure, so `lru4`'s 0% was unreadable; reason codes, capacity and working set now ride on every event

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): per-layer K is CORRECT and maximally valuable at small K (+1.96 pp at K=1) — but K=2 does not fit at 8 GB/262k at all, and the row cache's real currency is PROMPT LENGTH: a K=1 cache costs 69% of the maximum prompt

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): the owner's simpler rule ("in-flight wait, queued don't") is ALREADY implemented in the row-set path — and the real PP loss is a flag-off registration stall of~1.8-2.0 s, which also CORRECTS the disk-paging attribution above

## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): the proposed byte-accurate PCIe ledger is WITHDRAWN as unnecessary — byte accounting already exists, is free, and is exact; and the owner's mmap disk-paging worry is REAL, already measured, and costs 10.7-11.1% of the first PP pass
## 2026-10-02 (host-only, NO GPU): the 42.6% vs 4.0% conflict was a CATEGORY ERROR — they are disjoint terms, both true, and in the CURRENT run host execution is 52.2%, not 42.6%

## 2026-10-02 (expert row-cache K, host-only, NO GPU): per-layer K is worth at most +2 pp over flat K, the 8 GB target has NEGATIVE headroom for any cache, and a 215 us fixed cost per fetch is why 115x fewer bytes took 16x MORE time

## 2026-10-02 (T-GPLR-71 dip REPLICATION, one mutex hold, 12 interleaved arms): the ctx-131,072 dip DOES NOT REPRODUCE — it was a single-arm transient, and in ab21 the control's outlier was a DIFFERENT context

## 2026-09-23: PREDICTOR SCREENING PORTED FROM THE COLIBRI FUNNEL - coact/markov-1 beat the history baseline at every budget on every substantive stream, and coupling-copula leads unique coverage and high-budget recall (host-only, no GPU, no engine change; feasibility result, NOT a wire-in verdict). The T-GPLR-15 close left the predictive hypothesis explicitly open (ceiling 0.9385 vs retention 0.3088 at K=1); the colibri/deepseek-v4-baseline predictor-funnel (docs/findings/predictor-funnel-findings.md, DeepSeek-V4) supplied the candidate families and the replay methodology, now ported to our rowset_fetch schema as `tools/predictor-screen-gplr.py` (selftest for online faithfulness included, PASS; a predictor for (t,L) sees only tokens <t and layers <L, matching what the live engine could know). Corpus: 74 traces collapse to 7 distinct demand streams; screened one per stream (the two 256-token vehicles echo/honest, 50k-context, QA-depth; the two gplr57 rungs carry 3 TG tokens each and are reported but unconcludable). **Anchors:** history@B=8 reproduces the recorded (b) K=1 to ~1e-3 on BOTH vehicles (echo 0.3076 vs 0.3088; honest 0.2458 vs 0.2468) - the port is validated against the repo's own recordings; other shapes print anchor N/A (no recorded K=1; the first run mis-flagged 50k and the anchor was scoped to the 10240-row vehicle). **Results (recall@B / precision-per-byte / extra-hits-vs-history):** echo stream coact 42.6/43.0/16573 at B=8 vs history 30.8/30.9/0, markov-1 39.5, coupling-copula 31.9 but highest unique coverage and 77.2 recall at B=32; honest stream coact 28.1/28.4 at B=8 vs history 24.6 (same-precision +3.5pp), coupling 59.0 at B=32; 50k and QA streams repeat the ranking (coact/markov above history at every B, coupling wins B=32). **Reading:** colibri's H1 (same-layer transition structure beats history) and H2 (cross-layer coupling adds coverage, favors long context) both reproduce on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B; projection (labeled arithmetic, NOT measurement): a predictor feeding a K=2-sized window plausibly reaches what K=4-6 retention delivers - the charter's VRAM objective has a candidate lever. **Limits:** n=1 prompt per stream, no fresh capture; the (b)-projection is not a measurement; colibri's own T-pf-06 end-to-end A/B shrank fusion gains to noise on larger samples and its slot-thrash incident (UPDATE101) showed predicted fills must yield to exact demand - any wire-in needs that invariant plus a pre-registered acceptance quantity. Evidence: `docs/findings/predictor-screen-gplr.md` (method, full tables, reproduce commands); tool `tools/predictor-screen-gplr.py`; deterministic re-run verified. **Same-day extension (confidence-bar frontier + fusion, all offline):** colibri's barsweep/fusion operators ported (`--mode bar`, `--mode fusion`; selftest extended and PASS). Bar sweep: a conservative bar (0.9) strictly DOMINATES history on both axes on both streams (markov-1@0.9 = 25.1/29.0 vs history 24.6/24.7 honest; 36.1/41.7 vs 30.8/30.9 echo), but loosening to bar 0.7 collapses recall ~2.7x for a precision jump (41-57pp) - colibri's H3-disconfirm reproduces, so the bar is risk control, not frontier-pushing. Fusion (tune/held 80/20 split, grid at B=8): fusion dominates every single candidate on BOTH axes on both streams (best held: 29.6/29.6 honest vote-fusion vs history 22.7/22.7; 48.8/48.8 tuned weighted vs 27.9/27.9 echo); the colibri portable weight vector lands within 0.1pp (honest) / 2.4pp (echo) of per-stream tuning, so no per-cell tuning is needed; and the NULL-SOURCE CONTROL exposes the pool-growth share - a history-clone alone lifts held history 22.7 -> 28.0, so the structure-attributable gain is +1.6pp (honest) / +6.3pp (echo), and any wire-in case must argue against the null row, not the history row. Three measured operating points now exist for a wire-in decision: unbarred coact (+3.5pp honest, equal ppb), bar-0.9 (+0.5/+4.3, risk-free), fusion (+6.9/+6.9 honest with the null caveat). The T-pf-06 lesson stands: an offline win is a hypothesis; the engine A/B remains the verdict instrument.
